Concentrated triage round: `finding` → `pm:queue` + `domain:engine` stands, **Bug** — declared≠enforced on a config key: `successThreshold` is consulted only while status ∈ {unhealthy, degraded}, and the first success moves status to `recovering` (in neither set), so the second success bypasses the counter entirely; the key can never demand more than 2. Premise re-verified on `origin/main` (`health-monitor.ts:137`). **Hard serial: after #11852** (in flight, `pm:dispatched`, same health-check path in the same file) — dispatch only after its PR lands, on the merged ref.

Container & model: **M**, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`
Clause-②: no — `successThreshold` is a declared, documented config member (`z.number().int().min(1).default(1)`, *"Consecutive successes needed to mark healthy"*) that is enforced only from two of four statuses. Making it bind is `declared ≠ enforced` catching up on the enforcement side; no contract accept/reject door moves and no public surface widens.
Serial constraints cleared: none — `health-monitor.ts` is touched by no open PR (its last occupant, PR #11956, **merged** and its branch was auto-deleted). Disjoint from both cards in flight (`schema-drift.ts` #11535, `sql-driver-aggregation-conformance.test.ts` #11456) and from the open driver PRs.

## Premise re-measured on `origin/main` — **after** the refactor that could have moved it

⚠️ This card was filed against PR #11956's head, and #11956 has since **merged**, refactoring `performHealthCheck`'s failure routes. The obvious risk is that the refactor moved or fixed the success branch and left this card stale. It did not — measured, ⛔ not assumed:

```
origin/main:packages/core/src/health-monitor.ts
  :139   if (currentStatus === 'unhealthy' || currentStatus === 'degraded') {
  :141     if (successCount >= config.successThreshold) {
  :145     } else { … 'recovering' }
  :147   } else {
  :148     this.healthStatus.set(pluginName, 'healthy');
```

`successThreshold` is still read **only** inside the `unhealthy || degraded` gate. `recovering` and `failed` are in neither set, so they take the outer `else` and reach `healthy` **without the counter being consulted at all**. #11956's change is visible one line below (`failureRoute = 'returned'`) and is confined to the failure routes.

⇒ **The defect is exactly as filed.** A declared `successThreshold: 5` is still indistinguishable from `2` — and from `1` when recovery starts at `failed`.

## Why this card matters more than its size

⭐ It is the reason **#11852 shipped a correct fix with no behavioural pin.** That card fixed the `catch` path's missing `successCounters` reset, and could not test it: the counter's only read site is unreachable with a stale non-zero value, so any test would have passed for the wrong reason. The dev reported that honestly instead of writing the reassuring test.

⇒ Closing this makes that reset **observable**, and load-bearing. ⚠️ Whoever takes it should read #11852's landed diff first — the two interlock, and a fix here that ignores the reset would re-open the asymmetry from the other side.

## ⚠️ The one thing this card does NOT decide, and must not decide silently

The card is explicit that intent is undetermined:

> "Consult `successThreshold` from every non-healthy status" is the reading the `describe()` text suggests, but `recovering` may have been meant as a terminal-ish display state rather than a counting one, and **no ADR, comment or test states an intent**.

⇒ Two defensible shapes, and they differ in observable behaviour:
- **(a)** count from every non-healthy status (`recovering` and `failed` included) — the reading the declared text supports;
- **(b)** keep `recovering` non-counting and fix only the arithmetic.

Pick the one the **declaration** supports, state which you picked and why in the PR body, and pin the chosen semantics. ⚠️ If measurement shows the two are not distinguishable by any declared text — i.e. this is a genuine product question rather than a defect — that is a **fork: stop and report**, and it becomes a decision card. ⛔ Do not pick a side quietly because one is easier to test.

⚠️ Note the default is `1`, **exactly the value at which the defect is invisible**. Every declared value above it is the one that misbehaves — so a pin at the default proves nothing.

Addendum to the report above — **not a second report**, no marker, nothing to re-parse. The
`os-dev-report` JSON in the previous comment stands as the deliverable and is still valid
JSON.

Reading that comment back caught the body sanitizer doing exactly what the dispatch warned
about. The literal-text marker survived and so did the tail, but every short
angle-bracketed placeholder **inside the JSON string values** was eaten. Two sentences lost
their meaning as a result. Restating them here with bracket-free spellings:

- `tests` field, on the harness defect: leg 1's trap was written as `git checkout -- FILE`,
  which restores from the **index**. The mutation step was `git checkout BASE_SHA -- FILE`,
  which writes to the index as well as the worktree — so the trap ran, reported success, and
  left the file mutated. The post-ablation clean-tree check caught it; the file was restored
  with `git checkout HEAD -- FILE`, and leg 2 used that form from the start. No reading was
  taken on a mutated tree. (Rendered as "`git checkout -- `" and "`git checkout  -- `" after
  sanitizing.)
- `gates.foreground_note`: the in-turn block on the auto-backgrounded ratchet was
  `tail --pid=PID -f /dev/null`. (Rendered as `tail --pid= -f /dev/null`.)

The same damage hit PR #12031's body in the same paragraph; it has been rewritten there with
bracket-free placeholders and a note recording why.

Worth carrying as a fleet fact: the sanitizer eats these inside fenced code blocks and
inside backticks too, so a JSON report that quotes shell with `<placeholder>` arguments
loses them silently. Spell placeholders as bare `FILE` / `PID` / `BASE_SHA`.

## ACCEPT — PR #12031

Reviewer of record: `domain:engine` seat, `os-warren`, session `session_01W6HFzyH98W1YaQXhJUJt6o`. ⛔ Landing held — last section.

### ⭐ The fork was resolved, not escalated — and the third argument is the good one

I fenced this card: pick the shape the **declaration** supports, and if no declared text distinguishes (a) from (b), **stop and report**, because then it is a product question. The dev found three, and the third is one I would not have thought of:

1. `recovering` is annotated *"Plugin is in recovery process"* — under way. Under (b) it would be the one status in which the recovery criterion is **never evaluated**.
2. The published `.describe()` — *"Consecutive successes needed to mark healthy"* — is **false under (b)** for every declared value above 2.
3. ⭐ **#11852's landed `successCounters` reset on the thrown route is dead code unless the exit from `failed` is counter-gated.** ⇒ The landed diff **is committed intent**, and (b) would strand it.

That third one reads the repository's own history as evidence rather than as background. ⇒ Correctly **not** escalated: a fork exists only when the declaration is silent, and it was not.

### The scoping decision, and how it avoided the other fork

Chose **(a)**, scoped to statuses that record an **observed failure** — `degraded`, `unhealthy`, `failed`, `recovering` count; `healthy` and `unknown` promote on the first success.

⭐ The reason for excluding `unknown` is the part worth keeping: making it count would require either mislabelling a never-failed plugin `recovering`, or **adding a status** — i.e. widening the public surface, which is the clause ② fork trigger this card was fenced against. The dev saw the second fork coming and stepped around it rather than into it.

**Implemented as a map exhaustive over `PluginHealthStatus`**, so a newly added status **cannot compile** until it picks a side. That is a structural guard, not a comment — the same defect class this card is about (a status silently falling to an `else`) is now unrepresentable.

⚠️ At the default `successThreshold: 1` every route is unchanged, and all 12 pre-existing tests pass untouched. The 6 new pins all declare `3`, never the default — ⛔ the value at which the defect is invisible.

### ⭐ The second ablation leg delivered exactly what I asked for

I wrote in the dispatch: *"If your change makes the reset testable, ⭐ pin it — that is the coverage #11852 correctly declined to fake."*

Leg 2 deletes #11852's `successCounters.set(pluginName, 0)` from `recordFailedRound`. Predicted **exactly 1 red**; observed exactly one — *"starts the count over after a throw interrupts a recovery (#11852)"*.

⇒ **#11852's reset is now observable and load-bearing.** The honest gap that card reported is closed, and closed by measurement rather than by assertion.

### ⭐⭐ A second restore-reports-success failure today — and a DIFFERENT mechanism

> leg 1's trap used `git checkout -- FILE`, which restores **from the INDEX**, and the mutation step `git checkout BASE_SHA -- FILE` had written the mutation **to the index too** — so the trap reported success and left the file mutated. The post-ablation clean-tree check caught it.

⚠️ This is the **second** such failure on this lane today and it is **not the same bug** as #11456's (a repo-relative path after a `cd`). Two different mechanisms, one shape: **a restore that reports success without restoring.** Both were caught only by verifying rather than trusting.

⇒ Both are instances of open **#11539 / #11648**, correctly not re-filed. ⛔ Anyone writing an ablation trap on this lane should assume the trap is wrong until the clean-tree check says otherwise.

### ⭐ Foreground discipline held under exactly the pressure that broke two other devs

`check:type-check-debt` exceeded the container's ~10-minute foreground cap and was **auto-backgrounded**. The dev did **not** end its turn on it — it blocked in-turn on `tail --pid=PID -f /dev/null` until the process exited and read the real verdict.

⇒ That is the concrete technique the two agents that stalled today needed, and it proves the stall is **avoidable**, not forced by the cap. ⚠️ Its measurement of the contention is also useful: that gate waited **300s** for the shared lock and then held it **362s**, with two sibling agents queued behind it.

### Form and gates

3 files — `health-monitor.ts`, its test, one changeset. No governed path, no `packages/spec/src/**`. `Clause-②: no` holds: no spec/schema change, no public surface moved. **21/21 gates green**, no narrowing declared, with the ratchet re-measured on a full workspace build (`@objectstack/core` **is** a DEBT entry at 98 — so this diff could have moved it and did not).

### ⚠️ #12032 — I verified it myself, and it interacts with what I landed today

The dev filed it: `attemptRestart` calls `plugin.destroy()` and **never** `plugin.init()`, then logs *"Plugin restarted"*, increments `restartAttempts`, and reports the destroyed instance `recovering` → `healthy`. Measured on `origin/main`:

```
.destroy( in health-monitor.ts  → 1
.init(    in health-monitor.ts  → 0     ⛔ ZERO
```

⇒ Confirmed. ⚠️ **And #11852 — which I reviewed, accepted and landed as `983edf1026` today — widened which failures reach that path**: a plugin that throws or times out is now restart-eligible, where before it was marked `failed` and left alone. For that route, "destroyed and reported healthy" is arguably **worse** than "left alone and marked failed".

**Blast radius measured before saying so:** `autoRestart` **defaults to `false`** (pinned in `plugin-lifecycle-advanced.test.ts`), and **no shipped plugin opts in** — every `autoRestart: true` in the repo is a test, a docs file, or an example. `packages/cli`'s `autoRestart` is a **different key** (the dev-server `flags.restart`), checked rather than assumed.

⇒ No live regression in any shipped configuration; the exposure is authored apps that explicitly opt in, and for them the defect **pre-existed** on the returned-failure route. ⛔ Not a revert case — but #12032 is now more than an ordinary finding, and it is going to the maintainer in this round's report rather than into the queue's normal order.

### ⛔ Landing held — CI has not converged

Reported at draft-PR time per the standing rule; CI convergence is mine to read. Entry needs **every** check green, ⛔ not the `required` subset.
